prompt: Match each source of bias to an example.

pairs.right: past offers went to one region, so it looks loyal
one region is 4% of the training data
days since the last order means something else where deliveries are slow
a churn score is reused to choose who joins a club

right_distractors: a model trained with too few iterations

prompt: In this lesson's sense, when is a model biased?

choices.text: When its author intended to treat a group differently
choices.why: Bias needs no intent.

choices.text: When its errors fall more heavily on one group
choices.why: Right. Intent is not required.

choices.text: When its overall accuracy is below 80%
choices.why: Overall accuracy hides it.

choices.text: When it uses a sensitive column such as race or religion among its inputs
choices.why: The churn model used none and was still biased.

prompt: Flagged customers get an offer and stay. Next year's model learns that customers like them stay. What is this?

choices.text: A feedback loop
choices.why: Right. The model learns from behaviour its own decisions caused.

choices.text: Representation bias, since the flagged customers are a small share of everybody in the data
choices.why: Their number is not the issue.

choices.text: Overfitting
choices.why: That is memorising the training set.

choices.text: A leak
choices.why: No input contains the answer.

prompt: Under the loyalty club, which error is the harm?

choices.text: A missed churner
choices.why: Under the club, they get in; that is not a harm to them.

choices.text: Low accuracy
choices.why: Accuracy mixes both errors.

choices.text: A high threshold
choices.why: The threshold is fixed at 0.2 here.

choices.text: A false alarm: a loyal customer kept out
choices.why: Right. Being flagged now closes a door.

prompt: Of the North's 100 loyal customers, how many were flagged as leavers at 0.2?
A false-alarm rate of 20% rests on 100 customers. What is its margin of error, 1.96 standard errors, in percentage points? One decimal.
The North's recall is 58.8% against 66.7% in the Southeast. What can be concluded?

choices.text: The model misses the North's leavers
choices.why: 17 people cannot show it.

choices.text: The model favours the North, since it flags that region more often than any other in the table
choices.why: Being flagged more is the problem under the club.

choices.text: Nothing yet: it is ten of 17 people
choices.why: Right. A difference that small on 17 is noise.

choices.text: Recall is the wrong measure in general
choices.why: It is the right one for an offer.

prompt: Why did lesson 17's overall numbers show nothing wrong?

choices.text: Lesson 17 used the wrong threshold for the decision it was making about offers
choices.why: The threshold is not why it is hidden.

choices.text: The North is 117 of 2,558 customers
choices.why: Right. A small group vanishes in the average.

choices.text: The North has no false alarms
choices.why: It has 22.

choices.text: Overall numbers are computed on the training set
choices.why: They came from the test.

prompt: What makes the model see the North's loyal customers as fading?

choices.text: Their slower ordering rhythm
choices.why: Right. Deliveries arrive a week later, so orders are a week apart more.

choices.text: The region column, which the model weighs against them
choices.why: Region was not an input.

choices.text: They spend less per order than customers in other regions
choices.why: Spend was not an input either.

choices.text: They signed up more recently
choices.why: Nothing in the audit shows that.

prompt: Recency is correct for every North customer, yet the lesson calls it biased. Why?

choices.text: The dates were recorded in another time zone
choices.why: Every date is correct.

choices.text: Recency should be measured in weeks
choices.why: The unit changes nothing.

choices.text: The North has missing orders, so its recency is overstated by a few days for many customers
choices.why: No orders are missing.

choices.text: Eleven days of silence means something else there
choices.why: Right. The number is right; reading it as engagement is not.

prompt: Before building a fix on 'deliveries reach the North a week later', what should the analyst do?

choices.text: Nothing; the median gaps already prove the reason beyond doubt
choices.why: They show the rhythm, not why.

choices.text: Drop the North from the data
choices.why: That hides the problem.

choices.text: Ask logistics whether it is true
choices.why: Right. The reason for the rhythm comes from outside the data.

choices.text: Retrain with more iterations
choices.why: The model converged.

prompt: An input that carries a group's identity without naming it is a ___.

choices.text: leak
choices.why: A leak carries the answer.

choices.text: proxy
choices.why: Right. Recency was one for the North.

choices.text: residual
choices.why: That is what a model leaves unexplained.

choices.text: confounder
choices.why: Close in spirit, but the lesson's word is another.

prompt: A colleague proposes deleting the region column from every table so no model can be biased by region. What is the strongest objection?

choices.text: Without it the audit cannot be run
choices.why: Right. And the proxies still carry region.

choices.text: Region is needed as an input
choices.why: It was never an input.

choices.text: Deleting data is illegal under the LGPD
choices.why: The LGPD does not forbid it.

choices.text: The model would lose accuracy, since region is one of the strongest predictors of churn at Panela
choices.why: The North churns about as much as the rest.

prompt: Which of these commonly act as proxies for a person's income?

choices.text: Postcode
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The device they use
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The order ID
choices.why: It is assigned in sequence.

choices.text: The day of the experiment
choices.why: That says nothing about a person.

prompt: For the retention offer of lesson 17, which rate has to be equal across regions?

choices.text: The false-alarm rate among stayers
choices.why: That is the club's measure.

choices.text: The flag rate
choices.why: It ignores who actually leaves.

choices.text: Accuracy, which balances every kind of error into one number that people can compare
choices.why: One number hides which error hurts.

choices.text: Recall
choices.why: Right. The harm is a leaver who gets no offer.

prompt: Two groups churn at different rates. What does the mathematical result in the lesson say?

choices.text: A fair model needs equal churn rates
choices.why: It says which measures can be equal, not that none can.

choices.text: Every measure can be equalised by choosing the threshold carefully enough for each group
choices.why: That is what the result rules out.

choices.text: Equal precision rules out equal false alarms and recall together
choices.why: Right, unless the model makes no mistakes.

choices.text: Flag rate is the only valid measure
choices.why: It misleads here.

prompt: Reusing a model for a new decision means running the ___ again.
Put the steps of checking a model for bias in order.
items: name the decision the model will drive
say which error that decision turns into harm
compute that error rate per group, with margins
look for the cause in the inputs
confirm the cause with the people who know the business
